about: Human face signals (MediaPipe blendshape scores, 0..1) -> robot expression controls.
Each control is  clamp( sum over terms of  gain * deadzone( (score - neutral) / (1 - neutral) ) ).
neutral   = the score recorded during neutral calibration (set "baseline": false to skip it)
normalize = the division by (1 - neutral): resting scores are far from 0 (browDown rests near 0.4
on some faces), so this makes 'from your neutral to the maximum' the full 0..1 range
deadzone  = ignore changes smaller than this, so tracker noise cannot move a plate
gain      = exaggeration; robot motion should be bigger than the human movement behind it
{S} is the robot side (L/R) and {Side} the matching human side (Left/Right).
With camera.mirror on, the two are swapped so the avatar acts like a reflection.
Source names are the exact category names MediaPipe 1.0 returns (see README).
Note: cheekSquintLeft/Right read 0 with the current MediaPipe model; the smile and
eye-squint terms are what actually lift the cheeks.
